brief.summary: Swarm Defense builds small drones, and the software that lets one operator fly several of them, in Auburn Hills, Michigan. Products include the Kiwi, a quadcopter ordered in a one-way attack configuration, and target drones for counter-drone training. It says it grew out of Firefly Drone Shows, a light-show drone maker.
brief.thesis: Swarm Defense announced a minimum $25 million Department of War order for 4,000 Kiwi attack drones. The only equity on record is $1,435,000. The company says its swarm control software was developed over eight years of drone light shows.
brief.stage: A Form D filed 17 April 2026 reports $1,435,000 of equity sold to 10 investors (one non-accredited) and names none. FPDS shows $1,174,176 obligated across three awards. The company won no delivery order after Gauntlet I, placed fifth in Gauntlet II deep strike, and announced the minimum $25 million, 4,000-drone prototype order on 22 September 2026. It was not in FPDS on 2 October 2026.

On the Kiwi order, what is the delivery schedule, who supplies the munitions, and how much of the roughly $6,250 per drone stays with Swarm Defense?
What is actual monthly output today? The February 2026 release says capacity of 72,000 units a year, and a March 2026 WNEM report says 12,000 a year.

Delivering an armed product at this scale is unproven. The New York Times described October 2025 output as target drones under 2 pounds. The company gave no delivery schedule.

brief.summary: Deployable Energy Limited is a Houston company developing the Unity Nuclear Battery, a 1 MWe helium-cooled, water-moderated microreactor using 4.95% enriched uranium dioxide fuel. The company says units will be factory built and refuelled on a five-year cycle. A demonstration reactor completed a zero-power criticality test at Idaho National Laboratory on 30 June 2026.
brief.thesis: It reached criticality in roughly 150 days using 4.95% enriched fuel rather than HALEU. Its stated markets (defense, maritime, remote industry, data centers) and a Houston facility it says is intended for high-volume production fit energy, defense and manufacturing.
brief.stage: Solaris's 10-Q filed 6 August 2026 says it invested $5.0 million in June 2026 in a SAFE with a $150.0 million post-money cap. Deployable said on 17 August 2026 that Hornbeck Offshore also invested, amount not given. EDGAR shows no Form D. No source opened names other investors, a total raised or a priced round. The company told the NRC it plans a construction permit application by 1 December 2026.

brief.summary: Surtr Defense Systems builds ParallaxOS, described on its Y Combinator page as software that fuses data from radars, RF detectors, cameras and acoustic arrays into one picture, with a human in the loop. Tectonic describes an edge compute unit with software loaded, with weapon integration planned, not delivered. YC lists 2 people in San Francisco.
brief.thesis: Founder's pitch: militaries have stockpiled counter-drone sensors and effectors with no good way to integrate them, and Surtr wants to be the hardware-agnostic fusion layer. Tested in Ukraine through Brave1. Its FCC authority lists Fort Knox among radar test sites.
brief.stage: Formation stage. Tectonic reported on 7 July 2026 that Surtr, founded March 2026, raised a $4.8M pre-seed led by Allegis Capital, Eniac Ventures, Gaingels, Robinhood Ventures and Streamlined Ventures, giving no valuation or instrument. No Form D was found. Robinhood Ventures Fund II's N-2 and 10-Q list a $250,000 SAFE acquired 8 June 2026. The FCC granted an experimental special temporary authority for one radar on 3 September 2026.

questions: Which radars, RF sensors and effectors are integrated today, beyond the mic arrays and cameras Tectonic reported in July 2026, and how long does each new integration take?
What contract vehicle, if any, sits behind the Fort Knox and Point Defense Battle Lab testing, and is any of it paid? The FCC narrative names none.
The only instrument on record is a $250,000 SAFE. Is the whole $4.8M pre-seed on SAFEs, at what cap, and how much has closed?
Tectonic says Surtr is working on an ITAR licence to cue kinetic responses in Ukraine. Where does that stand, and what can Surtr do before it is granted?
risks: No source opened shows revenue or a contract. The FCC filings name no government contract, and Brave1 described the Ukraine work as a prototype test.
Early technical maturity. Tectonic reported in July 2026 that the software had so far been tested on mic arrays and cameras, with radars, passive sensors and turrets still to come.
Tectonic names Picogrid as already connecting these systems. The launch post says Surtr integrates with any hardware that has an API, so coverage depends on hardware makers exposing one.
unverified: The $4.8M total comes from the company's release to Tectonic. No filing confirms the total, valuation or terms beyond Robinhood Ventures Fund II's $250,000 SAFE.
Dealroom's body text says US$3.11M seed, citing Tectonic, while Tectonic says $4.8M pre-seed. The $3.11M figure is unexplained.
Founder statements in Tectonic, not confirmed by any government or third-party page: Point Defense Battle Lab testing approval, and latency under 100 milliseconds in the Kyiv tests.

Previously worked on neutrino physics with the NOvA experiment at Fermilab and on LHC experiments at CERN.

robocurve.description: Robocurve builds open-source tools and independent benchmarks to measure how well robots can do real-world jobs. Instead of relying on unverified demo videos from frontier labs, we score their models on reproducible benchmarks that anyone can trust. Today there are no well-run, standardized robotics benchmarks. Labs evaluate in-house, and no independent group has stepped in to run continuous benchmarking as a service. The result is that no one actually knows how good anyone else is, or where the real frontier sits. Good benchmarks require operating and maintaining physical hardware and real-world setups. Simulation only goes so far, since models that look strong in sim can show large performance gaps once deployed in the real world. Building real-world benchmarks means coordinating job-domain experts, evals engineering, and hands-on robotics all at once. Frontier labs are targeting general-purpose robotics by 2028, yet the field of robotics evals barely exists. Whoever builds the trusted measure of robot capability becomes the reference everyone relies on. We combine backgrounds in AI evals and robotics to build and grow this field as fast as possible. We already shipped v1 of our open-source framework, Inspect Robots, and ran our first pilot scoring a frontier model on a real robot.

brief.summary: Alva Energy develops extended power uprates for existing U.S. pressurized water reactors and plans to deliver them as fixed-price projects. brief.thesis: A project-delivery bet on reactors that already hold licenses. If the NRC accepts Alva's position on the balance of plant changes, the company says the same package could repeat across the U.S. fleet, which it puts at 10 GWe.
brief.stage: Alva announced a $33 million Series A on 12 February 2026, led by Playground Global. The release names investors from an earlier round without giving its size. An EDGAR full-text search for the company name returned no filings. It is in NRC pre-application, with a closed meeting set for 7 October 2026 on a topical report still listed as a draft. No source read names a utility customer.

unverified: The company says each uprate adds 250 to 300 MWe for about $1 billion, with first projects online in five years. No completed project backs these claims.

brief.thesis: Drones, counter-UAS, electronic warfare and directed energy all draw on the same tactical power supply. Chariot has a company-announced $7.6 million DIU contract to deliver to Army brigades, but the Series A is already done, led by Andreessen Horowitz.

What are unit price, gross margin and monthly output for Amphora 24 and Amphora 400, and who besides Adam Warmoth leads engineering and manufacturing?
risks: The round is recent and crowded. Andreessen Horowitz led the $34 million Series A in February 2026 with nine other named funds participating. No source gives a valuation.
Government money on record is small against $41 million raised. USAspending shows $74,900 obligated. The DIU contract rests on company releases, and no source names a program of record.

The amended Form C says predecessor Kean Wind Turbines ceased operations in 2019 following fundraising restrictions linked to a New York Attorney General investigation. What did it conclude?

risks: Very thin capital. Filings show $507,000 of seed preferred and $115,790.56 from Reg CF. Cash was $14,341.64 at 31 March 2026, and the amended Form C flags going concern doubt.

The IP is acquired and ageing. Both US patents were assigned by Kean Wind Turbines Inc., claim a June 2009 priority and expire in 2030 and 2032 per Google Patents.
unverified: The company claims letters of support from a US Air Force innovation officer and United Rentals (which it calls not final or binding). No letter was seen.
The SBIR phase and topic of the Air Force order are not confirmed from a primary source. HigherGov, an aggregator, lists SBIR Phase I. USAspending states no phase.
The New York Attorney General investigation into Kean Wind Turbines is known only from one sentence in the amended Form C. No Attorney General record was opened.

nori.description: We manufacture Nori: A sub-$2000 bimanual mobile manipulator that can clean rooms, restock shelves, and fold clothes. super-powers-mobility-spm.description: We started off building the highest performance, 470 volt electric off-road vehicles but we realized our ultra power dense battery packs are useful for mobile and stationary energy storage and power export, for military and consumer use cases. We develop battery packs, power electronics, and traction powertrain systems for vehicles. For the majority of 2026 we were marketing our electric off-road vehicles, but we pivoted to selling our high performance battery packs and power export capabilities in the month of September. We went from having $769,000 in consumer pre-orders (possibly low conversion rate to sales) to $421,815 in realized revenue in 1 month, with a $792,000 qualified pipeline. Our tech is so compelling because the safety and layout of high voltage battery packs has only been mastered by large, well funded OEM companies who have brought it in-house. That means all other companies without the in-house expertise rely on battery companies to develop packs, and power electronics companies to develop power export capabilities. SPM has both of those capabilities in-house so we can ensure a fast turnaround and much more reliable product. One of the biggest priorities of the department of war is energy dominance. We're seeing it constantly in new solicitations. Our strategy is superior - become a prime, but simultaneously service primes because most of then don't actually have the battery and power electronics expertise we have. Founded by Jon Powers - Ex-Tesla Sr. Mechanical Integration Engineer leading Cybertruck vehicle integration.

hundred.description: Hundred is an automated inspection system for the components that make up consumer devices like phones, smartwatches, and laptops. Hundred helps factories cut waste and prevent line-down issues by catching sub-100µm cosmetic defects before parts reach the assembly line. In the consumer electronics industry, designs change so fast that traditional machine vision can't keep up, forcing factories to rely on manual inspection, literally people checking parts under microscopes to sort out bad parts. Human inspectors miss roughly 15% of defects, and a single bad part can turn a finished device into scrap. Hundred is replacing manual inspection with an imaging rig that scans an entire shipping tray of parts at once. The Hundred rig blocks ambient light and uses varied controlled lighting configurations to detect defects smaller than 100µm on a range of materials. The controlled environment means Hundred only needs to scan a single good part before it can find defects, categorize them, and assess their severity accurately. Defects cost U.S. discrete manufacturers $45 billion a year, a problem Hundred's CEO, Erica, saw firsthand as a mechanical engineer designing devices at Meta, Google, and Magic Leap. She met Imani, Hundred's CPO, at Columbia University's admitted-students day in 2017 and Imani went on to spend five years at Twitch building software that handles billions of requests a day. Erica later met Iris, Hundred's CTO, in the Bay Area. Iris worked as a quant at Citadel before pivoting to study at Imperial College London where she researched machine learning on 3D meshes and other structured data. Together, they're building Hundred because manual inspection shouldn't still exist in 2026.

rodeo-robotics.description: Rodeo builds a robotic technician that automates maintenance so fleets can get vehicles back on the road sooner. Initial deployments focus on oil changes at centralized depots, where routine maintenance competes for scarce technician time. Cofounders Michael Hazard and Colby Duke met at Applied Intuition, where they worked with OEMs like Toyota and General Motors to bring software and autonomy to vehicles. They saw firsthand how much manual work it takes to keep vehicle fleets running, and learned how to make autonomy reliable through structured testing, real-world data, and human intervention. They’re now applying their experience to the roughly $600B annual US vehicle maintenance market. The average US vehicle is older than ever, driving up maintenance demand at a time when shops already struggle to hire and retain technicians. That gap leaves fleets facing costly downtime and preventable breakdowns. Despite this need, vehicle maintenance has resisted traditional automation. Service information is fragmented and unreliable, and vehicle hardware varies significantly between makes and models. Rodeo builds on advances in robotic foundation models to learn maintenance skills that transfer across vehicles. Rodeo pairs robots with human technicians who ensure each job is completed correctly, handling work the robots can’t yet perform autonomously. These deployments generate training data for Rodeo’s models through both teleoperation and hand tools augmented to record how technicians work. This lets Rodeo earn revenue while collecting the data needed to automate more of each job and improve margins.

facts.bio: Building robots for vehicle maintenance. Four years at Applied Intuition bringing software and autonomy to vehicles. Google APM. Stanford CS.
Building robots for vehicle maintenance. Previously the tech lead of Applied Intuition's neural simulation team.
